item.title: Trump says U.S. not to attack Iran before Nov. 3 midterms
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
A demonstrator holds a placard in front of the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States, on April 7, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Rui)
WASHINGTON, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- U.S. President Donald Trump said Thursday that the United States would not attack Iran before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, even as a U.S. blockade remained in place, while describing ongoing talks with Tehran as productive.
"We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd," Trump wrote on Truth Social.
"We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran," Trump said, adding that the country was in "very bad condition" economically and militarily.
He said the U.S. blockade would remain "in full force and effect," while claiming that 22 million barrels of oil had passed through the Strait of Hormuz overnight, with none coming from or going to Iran.
Trump concluded his post by declaring, "IRAN WILL NOT HAVE A NUCLEAR WEAPON!"
The Financial Times reported Thursday that oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz had fallen sharply, with preliminary data showing just 4 million barrels passing through on Tuesday, down from a weekly average of 15 million barrels per day in late September.
Before the United States and Israel launched a joint military campaign against Iran on Feb. 28, an average of 21.6 million barrels of oil passed through the strait daily in the final quarter of 2025, accounting for roughly one-fifth of global oil consumption, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

item.title: China warns Philippines to cease provocations, false claims
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
BEIJING, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- The China Coast Guard (CCG) on Thursday warned the Philippine side to immediately stop its infringements, provocations and false claims after a Philippine Coast Guard vessel transported an injured person from a grounded vessel near Ren'ai Jiao.
Jiang Lue, a spokesperson for the CCG, said that on Thursday, Philippine Coast Guard vessel 4409 went to waters near Ren'ai Jiao to transport one injured person from the vessel illegally grounded there.
Out of humanitarian considerations, the Chinese side immediately allowed the Philippine side to transfer the injured person by small boat, and the CCG handled the matter in accordance with the law and regulations, and provided necessary assistance, Jiang said.
The Philippine side's relevant remarks disregard the facts and distort the truth in an attempt to mislead the public, Jiang added.
China has indisputable sovereignty over the Nansha Qundao, including Ren'ai Jiao, and the adjacent waters, he noted.

item.title: Holiday travel, spending boom mirror vitality of China's vast market
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
BEIJING, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- From bustling transport hubs and crowded scenic areas to fully booked restaurants and busy shopping districts, strong travel flows and vibrant consumption during the National Day holiday highlighted the resilience and momentum of China's holiday economy.
Data from the Ministry of Transport showed that during this National Day holiday from Oct. 1 to 7, known as "Golden Week," cross-regional passenger trips reached 2.14 billion, averaging 306 million a day, slightly above the daily average recorded a year earlier.
Longer breaks, richer local experiences, rising inbound travel and policy-supported consumption... What stood out this year was not just the sheer number of travelers, but how the holiday economy was changing shape.
LONGER JOURNEYS, DEEPER EXPERIENCES
With the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays separated by only three working days this year, some travelers took three days of leave to link the two breaks into a 13-day extended holiday. Data from Trip.com Group showed that one in every 10 travelers combined the two holidays into such a break.
That extra stretch has helped reshape travel preferences, driving demand for longer-distance trips, a more relaxed pace and more immersive experiences.
Online travel platform Qunar said bookings for flights covering more than 2,000 kilometers rose by more than 40 percent year on year during the National Day holiday, while hotel bookings involving stays across four or more cities jumped 53 percent year on year.
Improved transport links are making long-distance trips more accessible than ever. Before the holiday, new high-speed rail sections, including the Xiong'an-Shangqiu, Xi'an-Ankang, and Harbin-Yichun lines, began operation, connecting more destinations across the country.
For families like Wang Lei's from Harbin, who traveled to Yichun to enjoy the autumn scenery, a journey that once took seven hours now takes just over one hour. "The time we used to spend on the road can now be spent enjoying the destination," Wang said.
Experts said longer breaks extend the consumption chain and expand spending opportunities, giving transport, hospitality, catering and scenic spots a longer operating window and deeper spending potential.
Official data showed that during the National Day holiday, average daily sales in service sectors rose 19.5 percent year on year, with tourism, sightseeing and entertainment services up 23.6 percent, catering services up 9 percent, cultural and arts services up 20.9 percent, and sports services up 29.4 percent year on year.
A noticeable shift unfolded during this year's National Day holiday: more travelers are looking beyond big-name cities and turning to smaller counties for their getaways.
In Mile City, southwest China's Yunnan Province, tourist Chen Jinhui from Shanghai in east China ordered a cup of local coffee and joined a community concert. "Coming to a small city, basking in the sun and relaxing -- that's the Yunnan way of life," he said.
Data from Qunar showed that hotel bookings in popular counties rose 32 percent year on year, with Jiuzhaigou County in southwest China's Sichuan and Burqin County in northwest China's Xinjiang among the most sought-after destinations.
In August, nine government departments, including the Ministry of Commerce, jointly issued guidelines to energize lower-tier markets and boost county-level consumption. The measures aim to streamline consumption channels, broaden the range of available brands, improve service quality, and create diverse and locally tailored consumption experiences in smaller cities and towns.
Small counties are no longer marginal players in the consumption landscape; they are becoming an important source of new domestic demand. McKinsey has projected that by 2030, more than 60 percent of China's personal consumption growth will come from third-tier cities and below, as well as county and rural markets.
Inbound tourism also remained robust during the holiday. Data from the National Immigration Administration showed that during the holiday, 682,000 foreign nationals entered China, of whom 505,000 arrived under visa-free policies, up 5.4 percent and 9.2 percent, respectively, from a year earlier.
As October arrives, autumn colors are spreading across Zhangjiajie National Forest Park in central China's Hunan Province. Tourists of different nationalities can be seen pausing for photos, listening to guides explain the area's unusual landscape, or watching local Tujia ethnic performances.
"Zhangjiajie is beautiful. We walked through the forest, felt close to nature, and it was very relaxing," said Noah, a tourist from Germany. He said he was especially impressed by the Tujia intangible cultural heritage performances and that the warmth of the local people made the visit truly memorable.
POLICY TAILWINDS, SMARTER SPENDING
Strong storefront demand and supportive policies are boosting consumption momentum. In the first six days of the National Day holiday, foot traffic and revenue at 78 major shopping streets and commercial districts monitored by the Ministry of Commerce rose 2.5 percent and 4.7 percent year on year, respectively.
Notably, the government's consumer goods trade-in program drove 33.48 billion yuan (about 4.97 billion U.S. dollars) in sales over the same period, benefiting 6.39 million consumers.
"During the holiday, we bought a new refrigerator. The subsidy saved us more than 1,000 yuan," said a Tianjin resident surnamed Wang.
The National Development and Reform Commission said before the holiday that it, together with the Ministry of Finance, had allocated the fourth and final batch of 62.5 billion yuan in ultra-long special treasury bonds for consumer goods trade-in programs, bringing this year's total to 250 billion yuan.
Data from the Ministry of Commerce showed that from Oct. 1 to 6, sales of embodied AI robots on key platforms surged 130 percent year on year, while sales of smart glasses doubled.
In Huaqiangbei, a sprawling electronics marketplace in south China's tech hub Shenzhen, new robots, AI translators and other tech gadgets have become popular purchases among foreign tourists.
"The number of overseas visitors has clearly increased. Most of them are buying tech products. Many come empty-handed and leave with full suitcases," said a local shop owner.
More international travelers are flocking to China to experience the country firsthand, riding a rising wave of global fascination with everything from the scenery and culture to its lifestyles and, more recently, Chinese brands and design.
From "China Travel" to "China Haul," the trend not only shows how Chinese manufacturing and innovation are winning over global visitors, but also confirms the potential and resilience of China's vast domestic market, supported by visa-free entry, expanded duty-free shopping and improved tax refund services for international visitors, said Zou Yunhan, a researcher with the State Information Center.

item.title: China remains committed to letting market play decisive role in determining exchange rate: central bank
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
BEIJING, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- China remains committed to letting market forces play a decisive role in determining the RMB exchange rate, the country's central bank said on Thursday.
The People's Bank of China (PBOC) stressed in a statement outlining its view on the RMB exchange rate that the country adopts a managed floating exchange rate regime based on market supply and demand with reference to a basket of currencies.
The RMB has moved in both directions since the country's exchange rate regime reform in 2005, said the central bank.
In bilateral terms, the RMB has strengthened against the U.S. dollar from 8.27 per dollar in July 2005, when the reform was launched, to around 6.7 per dollar recently, appreciating by 23 percent cumulatively.
In multilateral terms, the RMB nominal effective exchange rate calculated by the Bank for International Settlements has appreciated by over 50 percent since the exchange rate regime reform in 2005, while its real effective exchange rate up by 35 percent, according to the PBOC.
Since 2025, the RMB has strengthened by about 9 percent against the dollar. In particular, while non-dollar currencies have weakened broadly amid surging dollar index and Treasury yields since 2026, the RMB has extended its upward trend against the dollar.
"China has no need or intent to gain competitive advantages through currency devaluation, nor has it ever resorted to competitive devaluation," said the central bank.
China's trade growth is driven by its growing industrial competitiveness in the global market, said the central bank.
Exchange rate dynamics are driven by a number of factors including economic growth, monetary policy, financial market, geopolitics and sudden shocks, the PBOC said, adding that there is no straightforward relationship between the exchange rate and the current account.
Regarding global economic imbalances, the PBOC said in the statement that they are deeply intertwined with shifting global division of labor, inherent flaws in the international monetary system, and persistently high fiscal deficits and high consumption in some countries.
Addressing global imbalances requires collective actions from all stakeholders, according to the central bank.
"Attributing one's decline in industrial competitiveness, weakened fiscal discipline, and complicated structural issues simply to others' exchange rates is nothing but shifting the responsibility for adjustment onto others and dodging accountability," said the central bank.
A number of models for assessing the equilibrium exchange rate have emerged from academic studies over the years. Noting that there is no well-established methodology for evaluating the equilibrium level of exchange rates internationally, the central bank said "therefore, citing idiosyncratic assessment findings as 'official evidence' for RMB undervaluation is a misinterpretation and misuse of those findings."
The central bank said China has long been a contributor to global economic rebalancing. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), China will stay the course in transforming its economic growth model, expand domestic demand, improve the business environment, deepen high-standard opening up, and pursue a more open, inclusive and balanced global economy, the bank said.
Lu Lei, deputy governor of the PBOC, said in September that China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime, allowing market forces to play a decisive role in exchange rate determination while guarding against herd behavior and the self-reinforcing effects of irrational expectations.
In recent years, as China's export structure has undergone transformation and upgrading, companies have strengthened their pricing power and foreign exchange risk management capabilities, significantly reducing the sensitivity of China's trade to exchange rate movements, Lu said.
Meanwhile, foreign trade enterprises have increasingly used foreign exchange hedging instruments, while the RMB's share of trade settlement has continued to rise, further reducing the sensitivity of trade to exchange rate fluctuations, Lu added.
Guan Tao, chief economist at Huafu Securities, said that factors supporting both appreciation and depreciation of the RMB are currently at play.
In the short term, factors favoring a stronger RMB have the upper hand. Over the longer term, two-way fluctuations in the RMB exchange rate remain the norm, Guan noted.

item.title: Where the Long March began, China's new journey unfolds
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
An aerial drone photo taken on Aug. 18, 2026 shows a view of Yudu County, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Xinhua/Zhou Mi)
NANCHANG, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- The former ferry crossing is about half an hour's walk from the home of Sun Guanfa, 77, in Yudu, a hilly county in east China's Jiangxi Province.
For his father, the journey from this riverbank more than nine decades ago was part of an epic.
In October 1934, some 86,000 soldiers of the Red Army crossed the Yudu River to embark on what later came to be known as the Long March.
In a country beset by foreign invasion, social turmoil and destitution, the fledgling Red Army, led by the Communist Party of China (CPC), was fighting for national independence and the liberation of the Chinese people. But at the time, it was encircled by the overwhelming and much better-armed Kuomintang forces.
What followed was an epic military maneuver: from Yudu, Red Army troops trekked roughly 12,500 kilometers across China, crossing snow-covered mountains and treacherous marshlands, all the while battling enemy forces. They eventually reached the country's northwest, where, in 1936, they were joined by several other Red Army branches, marking the victorious conclusion of the Long March.
This military maneuver preserved the Red Army. It also gave the CPC a new foothold in northwest China, from which it built up its strength, fought back against invading Japanese troops and eventually toppled the corrupt Kuomintang regime, leading to the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949.
In Yudu, the Long March is not simply a chapter in a history book. It is a family story.
More than 17,000 residents joined the departing army. Only 277 were recorded as eventually returning home, said Zhong Min, a guide at a museum built beside the river to commemorate the departure.
Her voice still catches when she says that number.
Her maternal great-grandfather died fighting the encirclement campaigns. Her husband's grandfather marched away with the troops and was never heard from again. Sun's father fell in a battle that saw the forces of the Red Army reduced to just over 30,000.
"We are not telling other people's stories," Zhong said. "We are telling our own families'."
Here, the Long March is measured not only in kilometers and battles, but in the people who left home knowing they might never return.
For Sun, the legacy of that generation is deeply personal. Under a local tradition, Sun was adopted as the son of the soldier who left the riverbank and never returned, so that the soldier's family line could continue.
"People of my father's generation were willing to give their lives so ordinary people could be liberated," Sun said.
On the same riverbank in 2019, Chinese President Xi Jinping spoke of what had enabled the Party and the Red Army to come back from the brink of destruction time and again: firm ideals and convictions, and strong willpower.
"We must not forget our Party's original aspiration and founding mission," said Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission. The Party's long-stated mission, dating to its founding in 1921, is to seek happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.
During the visit, Xi placed a flower basket at a monument commemorating the Red Army's departure and bowed in tribute. He then walked behind the monument to a railing overlooking the river and stood there for a long while.
The river remains. For Xi, it was also a place from which to look ahead to China's future.
"We came to this place to revisit what it was like when the Red Army set out," he told local people gathered nearby. "Today we are on a new journey -- to build a modern socialist country. We must carry on the work of those who came before us, gear up anew, and set out once more."
That new journey was unfolding against a vastly changed backdrop. When Xi visited Yudu, the nationwide campaign he had launched to combat poverty was entering its final stage.
It would culminate in the elimination of absolute poverty in a nation of 1.4 billion. Nearly 100 million rural residents were lifted out of poverty under Xi's "targeted poverty alleviation" campaign, which mobilized the entire Party and the nation.
Xi announced the victory, as a key part of building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, in 2021 when the CPC marked its centenary.
A drone photo taken on Oct. 2, 2026 shows tourists at a memorial hall marking the departure of the Long March by the Central Red Army in Yudu County, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Photo by Zeng Xiaomao/Xinhua)
During his 2019 visit, Xi saw for himself whether the former revolutionary base areas were on track to meet their poverty-reduction targets.
At Sun's home, he walked through the main hall to the backyard and checked the kitchen and the bedrooms. There was rice and cooking oil in the kitchen, and the bathroom was clean.
Xi asked about the family's income and how Sun's son and daughter-in-law made a living, where their children went to school, and what the school meals were like.
"By the time they grow up, we will have achieved the rejuvenation of our nation," Xi said, pointing to Sun's two grandchildren.
China aims to basically realize socialist modernization by 2035 and build a great modern socialist country in all respects by the middle of this century, according to the vision set by the Party.
Earlier, at the museum where Zhong served as a guide, Xi had stopped before a map of China made from straw sandals.
The display recalled how local people worked through the night to make straw sandals for the soldiers, many of whom fought barefoot. They also dismantled doors, bed boards, roof beams and even timber intended for coffins to build pontoon bridges, helping the soldiers cross the Yudu River.
"The country has developed and people's lives have improved, but we must remember where it all came from," Xi said. "We must not forget our revolutionary forefathers and those who died for the revolution, or the people of the old revolutionary base areas."
Nowadays, golden waves of selenium-rich rice ripple around the 700-year-old village, and rows of modern vegetable greenhouses stand nearby. In the residential area, white-walled houses with gray-tiled roofs sit amid trees, while pavilions nestle between them.
"Now we have wages from working, rent from our guesthouses and dividends from our shares," Sun said. "Our annual income has tripled to more than 200,000 yuan (around 29,000 U.S. dollars)."
This file photo taken on Oct. 21, 2020 shows Sun Guanfa (L) introducing local agricultural products to tourists in Tantou Village, Yudu County, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Xinhua/Wan Xiang)
The transformation extends well beyond Yudu.
Much of southern Jiangxi, once cut off from the outside world by rugged mountains, is far more connected. High-speed rail links it with the city of Shenzhen, the country's economic powerhouse close to Hong Kong. Expressways also reach every county, and paved roads now extend into villages.
For local business owners, it no longer means spending two days and two nights on the road to source a critical part. Now they can hop on a high-speed train, pick up what they need in the morning and return that afternoon, drastically speeding up the development of a prototype.
The change is not only about getting around. Industries such as non-ferrous metals and advanced materials, electronics and information technology, and textiles and apparel have taken root here. For ordinary people, the changes are closer to home. Housing has improved, drinking water is safer, and schools and medical care are more accessible.
More people can now earn a living without leaving their hometowns. In March, the Hong Kong Polytechnic University launched a facility dedicated to research into smart wearables and smart clothing in Xingguo, a county next to Yudu.
This summer, Yudu welcomed students from more than 170 universities across China who came to retrace the Long March at the places where it began. Many realized that the Red Army soldiers who set out were their age.
"Standing where those young soldiers began their journey gave me a deeper understanding of what they accomplished," said Liu Fanshuo, an undergraduate studying automation.
Today, five modern bridges span the Yudu River near the crossings where local people once built pontoon bridges to help the Red Army cross.
On the banks, Sun pours hot tea for tourists whose lives might have been very different had those soldiers never crossed.

item.title: China's railways see holiday return peak amid vibrant tourism market
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Passengers are seen at the waiting hall of Tianjin Railway Station in north China's Tianjin, Oct. 7, 2026. As the National Day holiday is drawing to a close, return travel flows increase across the country. (Photo by Du Penghui/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Oct. 7 (Xinhua) -- China's railways saw the peak of the holiday return rush on Wednesday, with 24.15 million passenger trips expected on the final day of the National Day holiday, amid strong travel demand and vibrant tourism activity across the country.
A total of 2,449 additional passenger trains were scheduled on Wednesday to cope with the surge in demand, according to China State Railway Group Co., Ltd.
On Tuesday, the country's railways handled 21.6 million passenger trips, marking the third consecutive day with more than 20 million journeys.
Beijing, Guangzhou, Chengdu, Xi'an, Wuhan, Hangzhou, Chongqing and Shanghai were among the busiest cities for departures and arrivals, while passenger flows were particularly heavy on routes including Beijing-Shanghai, Wuhan-Shanghai, Wuhan-Shenzhen and Xi'an-Chengdu.
Railway authorities across the country added services and expanded overnight operations to facilitate the return rush as China's tourism market remained vibrant during the seven-day holiday, with county-level destinations and nighttime consumption emerging as notable trends.
County-level destinations gained popularity as travelers increasingly sought slower-paced and more immersive experiences away from major cities.
From the coastal county of Lingshui in south China's Hainan Province to Mohe, a county-level city on the country's northern frontier, smaller destinations are drawing visitors with distinctive local experiences.
Meanwhile, nighttime consumption flourished in many cities, with cultural performances, night markets, light shows and food fairs extending visitor stays and enriching holiday experiences.
Passengers are seen at the waiting hall of Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station in east China's Shanghai, Oct. 7, 2026. As the National Day holiday is drawing to a close, return travel flows increase across the country. (Xinhua/Ding Ting)
Passengers are seen at the waiting hall of Wuhan Railway Station in Wuhan, central China's Hubei Province, Oct. 7, 2026. As the National Day holiday is drawing to a close, return travel flows increase across the country. (Photo by Zhao Jun/Xinhua)

item.title: Another Nanjing Massacre survivor dies, only 20 remain
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Another survivor of the Nanjing Massacre died on Wednesday, reducing the number of registered living survivors to 20, the Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders said.
Massacre survivor Guo Xiulan died at the age of 94, according to the memorial hall in Nanjing, the capital of east China's Jiangsu Province.
Guo was born in 1932. According to survivor recollections documented by the museum, when the Nanjing Massacre took place after Japanese troops captured Nanjing on December 13, 1937, Guo's parents took their three children to hide in an underground shelter along with neighbors.
"Japanese soldiers stood at the opening and strafed it with machine guns. My parents and my youngest sister perished. Only my second sister and I survived," Guo was recorded as saying.
The Nanjing Massacre unfolded over six weeks. Japanese soldiers killed approximately 300,000 Chinese civilians and unarmed soldiers in one of the most barbaric atrocities of World War II.
Over the years, the number of survivors able to share firsthand accounts of the massacre has continued to decline.
In 2014, China's top legislature designated December 13 as the national memorial day for the victims of the Nanjing Massacre. The Chinese government has also preserved survivors' testimonies through written records and video recordings.
Documents related to the massacre were inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register in 2015. To date, only 20 living survivors of the Nanjing Massacre remain on the registry maintained by the Nanjing Association for Assistance to Victims of Japanese Aggression and Inheritance of Nanjing Massacre Historical Memory.

item.title: Immersive experiences fuel inbound tourism boom over China's National Day holiday
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Foreign tourists at the Palace Museum in Beijing, China, October 6, 2026. /VCG
China's inbound tourism market is seeing robust growth during the 2026 National Day holiday.
China's border crossings are expected to handle an average of about 2.15 million passenger trips per day during the holiday, according to the National Immigration Administration.
Data from Chinese online travel agency Trip.com showed that inbound tourist trips during the combine holiday posted double digit year-on-year growth for the first time.
New trends are emerging in China's inbound tourism market, as overseas visitors move beyond traditional sightseeing, and increasingly immerse themselves in local life, culture and experiences.
Orders for one-day inbound tours surged more than fourfold year on year, while scenic spot ticket bookings jumped over 220%. Cultural attractions accounted for around 43% of inbound scenic spot bookings during the combined holiday, up from about 32% in 2024.
Russian tourist learned black tea brewing in Huzhou, Zhejiang Province, China, June 5, 2026. /VCG
Traditional Chinese style photo shoots have also become a new source of tourism spending among foreign visitors. At Shanghai's Yu Garden, a popular destination for foreign tourists, they are dressing in traditional Chinese hanfu and taking ancient style photos against a backdrop of upturned eaves and traditional pavilions, embracing a new way to experience Eastern aesthetics.
Cultural performances are also offering foreign visitors new ways to experience and understand China. In Zhangjiajie, central China's Hunan Province, shows such as "Charming Xiangxi" blend intangible cultural heritage with real mountain and water scenery, modern lighting and multilingual subtitles. By the end of September, the "Charming Xiangxi" theater had welcomed more than 140,000 overseas visitors this year.
The "Charming Xiangxi" performance in Zhangjiajie, Hunan Province, China, October 4, 2026. /VCG
In Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, the Huaqiangbei electronics market has emerged as a popular tech shopping destination for overseas visitors, who are captivated by AI translation glasses, smartwatches, humanoid robots, portable AI speakers and panoramic cameras.
The surge in inbound tourism was fueled by China's expanding visa-free policies.
During this year's Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, from September 25 to 27, foreign nationals made 728,000 border crossings, up 37.7% year on year. Among inbound foreign visitors, a total of 247,000 entered under visa-free policies, an increase of 32.7% from a year earlier, data from the National Immigration Administration showed.
Foreign tourists arrive at Shanghai Pudong International Airport in Shanghai, China, September 30, 2026. /VCG
The growth in inbound travel is driven by the ongoing innovation in China's tourism offerings, experiences and consumption scenarios, giving international visitors more opportunities to engage with local culture and everyday life, said Li Xinjian, executive dean of the Capital Culture and Tourism Development Research Institute at Beijing International Studies University.
Li added that China is increasingly becoming a destination where travelers can not only see the sights, but also immerse themselves in the experience.

item.title: Flag-raising ceremony held at Tian'anmen Square to celebrate 77th founding anniversary of PRC
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
A flag-raising ceremony to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China (PRC) was held at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing on Thursday.
The Guard of Honor of the Chinese People's Liberation Army escorted the national flag to the square, while the military band played the national anthem.
Many people from across China gathered at the square to watch the ceremony.

item.title: Activities held across China to celebrate National Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Cities across China are decorating landmark sites with national flags and floral displays as National Day arrives, and people hold various activities to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
